title: If the maximal ideal is not an associated prime of a finite module, it contains a nonzerodivisor on it
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that $\mathfrak m$ is not an associated prime of $M$, i.e. there is no $z\in M$ with $\{a\in R: az=0\}=\mathfrak m$. Then there is an $x\in\mathfrak m$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $x$ on $M$ is injective).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor, line 15471), implication (2) => (1) for $I=\mathfrak m$ (for $I=\mathfrak m$ the condition $\mathfrak m\not\subset\mathfrak q$ for all $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ says $\mathfrak m\notin\operatorname{Ass}(M)$, as $\mathfrak m$ is maximal)

proof.text: Let $A=\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, the associated primes defined by annihilators as in the statement. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite], since $R$ is Noetherian and $M$ is finite. For every $\mathfrak q\in A$, the ideal $\mathfrak q$ is proper, hence $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$ because $R$ is local. By the hypothesis $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak m\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor, lines 15471-15494), condition (2) for I = m; Lemma Tag 00LC (lemma-finite-ass, line 15176)

proof.text: If $A$ is nonempty, list its distinct members as $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_r$ with $r\ge1$. Step 1 gives $\mathfrak m\not\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$ for each $i$, and each $\mathfrak q_i$ is prime. Prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance], applied to $J=\mathfrak m$ and the $\mathfrak q_i$, yields $x\in\mathfrak m$ outside every member of $A$. If $A$ is empty, take $x=0\in\mathfrak m$, which is also outside every member of $A$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor, lines 15486-15494), invoking Lemma Tag 00DS (lemma-silly, line 2563)

proof.text: The chosen $x$ belongs to no associated prime of $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], $x$ is therefore not a zerodivisor on $M$: if $xz=0$, then $z=0$. Thus multiplication by $x$ is injective. This also covers $A=\varnothing$: then the union of associated primes is empty, so even $x=0$ is regular on $M$ (necessarily $M=0$).
